memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground. He said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, do not pass your servant by. Let a little water be brought, and then you may all wash your feet and rest under this tree." - Gen 18:2b-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Watch how Abraham responds to these strangers. He "hurried" to meet them. He bowed low. He begged them to stay: "do not pass your servant by." At nearly a hundred years old, in the heat of the day, this dignified man runs to welcome travellers he does not even know. His eagerness to serve is remarkable.

This is the beautiful grace of hospitality - a heart open to the stranger, quick to serve, glad to share. In Abraham's world, welcoming travellers was sacred duty, but he goes far beyond mere duty. He is genuinely eager, treating these guests as an honour rather than an interruption.

There is deep instruction here for us. Our culture often treats people as interruptions to our real business. But Abraham shows us that welcoming others - especially the stranger, the traveller, the one with no claim on us - is a holy privilege, not a burden.

And there is a wonderful mystery: Abraham did not yet know these visitors carried the presence of God. Hebrews reflects on moments like this: "Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it" (Heb 13:2). When we welcome the stranger, we may be welcoming far more than we realise. Jesus said, "I was a stranger and you invited me in" (Matt 25:35). Open your door and your heart today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you treat people as interruptions or as opportunities to serve?
- Is your heart open to welcome the stranger?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me the eager, open heart of Abraham toward the stranger and the guest. Help me see hospitality not as a burden but as a holy privilege, welcoming others as I would welcome You.
Amen.
